sections.heading: A new situation
paragraphs: Dina was learning how to handle money and payment in everyday English. The goal was to communicate clearly and politely. Dina practiced “How much is the total?” A useful phrase was “I would like to pay by card.” A useful phrase was “Do you accept cash?” They repeated it to remember the meaning. Dina practiced “Can I use contactless payment?” A useful phrase was “The card machine is not working.” A useful phrase was “Let me try another card.” They repeated it to remember the meaning. Dina practiced “Please enter your PIN.” A useful phrase was “The payment went through.” A useful phrase was “Could I get a receipt?” They repeated it to remember the meaning.

sections.heading: Finding the right words
paragraphs: As the situation developed, Dina listened carefully and tried more useful expressions. Dina practiced “I think I was charged twice.” A useful phrase was “Let us check the transaction.” A useful phrase was “The refund may take a few days.” They repeated it to remember the meaning. Dina practiced “What is the price before tax?” A useful phrase was “Is the service fee included?” A useful phrase was “I need to stick to my budget.” They repeated it to remember the meaning. Dina practiced “I track my spending every week.” A useful phrase was “I am saving for a new laptop.” A useful phrase was “This purchase can wait.” They repeated it to remember the meaning.

sections.heading: Making a choice
paragraphs: There were more details to understand, so Dina slowed down and chose the next words thoughtfully. Dina practiced “Can we split the bill?” A useful phrase was “I will pay my share.” A useful phrase was “You can send me the amount later.” They repeated it to remember the meaning. Dina practiced “I transferred the money yesterday.” A useful phrase was “Have you received the transfer?” A useful phrase was “The bank app shows it is pending.” They repeated it to remember the meaning. Dina practiced “There is not enough balance.” A useful phrase was “I need to withdraw some cash.”

sections.heading: A confident finish
paragraphs: At the end of the activity, Dina reviewed the final expressions and felt more comfortable speaking. Dina practiced “Where is the nearest ATM?” A useful phrase was “The machine charges a small fee.” A useful phrase was “I would like to exchange some currency.” They repeated it to remember the meaning. Dina practiced “What is today's exchange rate?” A useful phrase was “Please count the change.” A useful phrase was “The amount seems correct.” They repeated it to remember the meaning. Dina practiced “I will keep a record of this payment.” A useful phrase was “Thank you, everything is settled.”
